answers.value: All engineering documentation pages in the Confluence 'Engineering Knowledge Base' space (and READMEs in the GitHub Enterprise 'platform-*' repos) whose 'Last reviewed' label is older than 12 months OR whose subject component has been decommissioned per the CMDB. Scope excludes regulatory/actuarial governance docs held in the model governance repository.
Documents last modified on or before 2025-06-30 (rolling 12-month lookback); archival run executed the first business week of each quarter.

Each archived page carries a 'Status: Archived' banner, a sunset date, and a link to the current replacement page (or 'No replacement - capability retired, CMDB CI xxxxx'). Pages missing a replacement reference are blocked from archival.
Count of pages moved to the 'Archive' space in Confluence equals the count on the archival worklist exported from the Jira epic; delta must be 0 before the run is marked complete.
Confluence page-version history plus the exported archival worklist CSV (with page ID, sunset date, replacement URL, archiver, ISO-8601 timestamp) attached to the Jira story and retained 3 years.

Any doc that cannot be archived (still linked from a live runbook, no owner, or replacement not yet published) is logged as a sub-task on the Jira epic with disposition 'Deferred - reason', owner = Backend Developer, 10-business-day resolution SLA.
Sample of 25 pages from the archival worklist plus a full sweep for any page still tagged 'current' but last reviewed > 12 months ago.

PASS = 100% of sampled archived pages have Archived banner + sunset date + valid replacement link, and 0 stale 'current' pages remain; FAIL if any archived page lacks a replacement reference or any stale current page is found.
Failures reopen the Jira story, assigned to Software Engineer with a 5-business-day fix SLA; recurrence > 2 quarters escalates to the Engineering Manager for a knowledge-management process review.
Confluence page metadata fields used: page ID, space key, 'Last reviewed' label, 'Owner' property, and the linked CMDB CI status (Active/Retired) that drives the sunset decision.
Reconcile total live+archived page count in the Engineering KB space before and after the run against the CMDB component inventory; no net loss of content, only status transitions.

Archival covers documents effective/last-reviewed on or before 2025-06-30; each archived page's effective sunset date is recorded in the Confluence 'Sunset' property and mirrored on the Jira worklist row.

answers.value: The change/release under review at the implementation gate: all pull requests targeting the release branch in GitHub Enterprise for the named Jira release version, together with the ADR(s) and design package attached to the Jira 'Design Gate' issue.
Gate decision applies to the current release cycle (2-week sprint / named release version); approval expires if the release is not deployed within 30 calendar days and must be re-granted.

Gate record captures: ADR link, design-vs-implementation conformance note, CI status (green), SAST/SCA status (0 critical/high), and named approver. All fields mandatory before the Jira gate transition is permitted.
Number of PRs merged to the release branch equals the number listed on the design package's scope table; any unlisted PR blocks approval until reconciled.
Signed gate decision recorded as a comment on the Jira 'Design Gate' issue with the approver's name, decision (Approve/Reject/Conditional), conditions, and ISO-8601 timestamp; retained 3 years.
Conditional approvals log each condition as a linked Jira sub-task with owner and due date; unresolved conditions at deploy time block promotion via the pipeline gate.

checklist.step: Require an ADR for the design decision at the gate
checklist.value: The Jira 'Design Gate' issue links an ADR in the repo /docs/adr folder covering the significant design choice under review.

testing.step: Confirm ADR presence and status before approval
testing.value: Gate cannot transition to Approved unless the linked ADR exists and is in 'Accepted' status; verified by a Jira automation rule.

checklist.step: Bind the gate to CI quality gates
checklist.value: Approval requires the release branch CI run to be green with SonarQube quality gate passed and 0 critical/high SAST findings.

testing.value: Cross-check the Jira gate record against the GitHub Actions run: an approval with a failed/absent quality gate is a control failure.

checklist.step: Enforce PR-based flow into the release branch

testing.step: Audit release-branch history for direct commits

checklist.value: Each PR in scope shows >= 2 approving reviews, at least one from a reviewer other than the author, per branch protection.

checklist.value: Gate checklist mandates completed threat-model review and passing SAST/SCA before approval, evidencing secure-development procedures.

testing.value: Sampled gate records include SAST/SCA reports with 0 unresolved critical/high findings or an approved SDLC-Exception ticket.

answers.value: All production Kafka topics and consumer groups in the streaming pipeline that feed the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse landing zone, plus the Flink/Spark Structured Streaming jobs that read them.
Continuous, 24x7 real-time monitoring; dashboards retain 90 days of metric history and alerts evaluate on 1-minute windows.
Every topic exposes consumer-lag, partition-skew, and end-to-end latency series to Prometheus; a topic missing any of the three required metrics is flagged red on the pipeline health dashboard.
Records produced to source topics reconcile with records landed in the lakehouse per 15-minute bucket within a 0.1% tolerance; sustained breach raises a P2 alert.

Grafana dashboard JSON is versioned in the source code/CI-CD repository; alert-firing history and on-call acknowledgements are retained in the alerting platform for 90 days and exported to the ITSM incident record.
Each threshold breach auto-creates a ServiceNow incident tagged 'streaming-pipeline'; disposition (resolved / false-positive / suppressed-with-reason) recorded on the incident before closure.
All in-scope topics/consumer groups over a representative peak-load window (e.g., the daily batch-catch-up spike) plus a synthetic lag-injection test on one non-prod topic.

PASS = consumer lag < 10,000 messages sustained, p99 end-to-end latency < 5s, and 0 partitions in a stalled state; FAIL if any metric exceeds threshold for > 5 consecutive minutes without a firing alert.

On alert, on-call SRE follows the linked runbook; if lag is unrecoverable within the 30-minute SLA, escalate to Software Engineer (owner) and open a P1 in ServiceNow with the consumer-group offset snapshot attached.

Acceptance: telemetry is 'observable' when lag, partition utilization, and end-to-end latency for every prod topic are live on the Grafana dashboard with at least one bound alert rule each and a 90-day retention window.
Grafana dashboard 'Streaming Pipeline Health' (folder: Data Engineering); alert rules and dashboard JSON stored at repo path /observability/streaming/ in the source code/CI-CD repository.

checklist.step: Bind monitoring and alerting to the pipeline
checklist.value: Consumer lag, partition utilization, and end-to-end latency each have a Grafana panel and a Prometheus alert rule with defined thresholds.

testing.value: Inject artificial lag on a non-prod topic; confirm the alert fires and an incident is created within 1 minute.

checklist.value: Rate, Errors, and Duration are surfaced per consumer group on the health dashboard sourced from Prometheus exporters.

testing.value: Every prod consumer group has non-null Rate/Errors/Duration series for the last 24h; missing series fail the check.

checklist.value: Each alert links a runbook and names an owning on-call rotation; no alert without a documented response.

testing.value: 100% of active alert rules resolve to a linked runbook URL; any orphan alert is remediated.

checklist.step: Enable distributed tracing across the pipeline
checklist.value: Trace/correlation IDs propagate from producer through Flink/Spark to the lakehouse sink, visible in the tracing backend.

testing.value: A sampled event ID is traceable from ingestion topic to lakehouse row with per-hop latency recorded.

answers.value: Every producer, topic, stream-processing job, and sink in the streaming pipeline within the named domain; documentation covers event flow, partitioning keys, schemas, and consumer groups.
Topology doc reflects the current release; refreshed on every schema/topology change and reviewed at least quarterly.

Topology doc includes, per topic: name, partition count, key strategy, producing service, consuming groups, schema subject, and retention. A topic present in the broker but absent from the doc fails the completeness check.
Topic count in the documented topology equals the live topic count from the Kafka admin API (excluding internal __consumer_offsets); delta must be 0.

Topology doc lives as a versioned Confluence page and a source-controlled diagram (Mermaid/C4) at /docs/streaming/topology in the source code/CI-CD repository, each carrying a version and last-updated timestamp.
Undocumented or orphaned topics discovered during reconciliation are logged as Jira tasks with disposition 'document' or 'decommission', owner = Backend Developer, 10-business-day SLA.
All prod topics and stream jobs in the domain, compared against the live broker/topic inventory.
PASS = 100% of live topics documented with all required fields and diagram reflects actual producer/consumer wiring; FAIL if any live topic is missing or a documented edge does not match runtime.
Discrepancies open a Jira 'doc-drift' task assigned to Software Engineer, 5-business-day fix SLA; the topology page is blocked from 'Approved' until drift = 0.

Field definitions sourced from the schema registry subjects (Avro/Protobuf) and the Kafka topic configs (partitions, retention, cleanup.policy); the doc references subject names and versions, not copied field lists.
Reconcile documented topic/partition totals against the Kafka admin API describe-topics output; totals must match exactly.

Acceptance: topology doc is complete when live-topic reconciliation delta = 0 and the C4/Mermaid diagram matches runtime wiring; evidence is the versioned Confluence page plus the diagram at /docs/streaming/topology in the source code/CI-CD repository.

checklist.value: A container/component-level C4 diagram of the streaming topology is version-controlled and embedded in the Confluence page.

testing.value: Producers/consumers on the diagram reconcile against live consumer-group metadata; mismatches fail.

testing.value: Automated diff of documented topics vs Kafka admin API returns 0 undocumented topics.

Every active topic has a registered subject with owner, description, compatibility mode, and business-glossary link populated in the catalog; a topic with data but no registered subject is a hard failure.
Count of registered subjects reconciles with count of active prod topics (1:key + 1:value where applicable); unmatched subjects/topics are listed for remediation, target delta 0.

All active subjects in the schema registry compared against active topics and against catalog entries.
PASS = 100% of active topics have a current, catalog-discoverable subject with required metadata and a set compatibility mode; FAIL if any subject is orphaned, stale, or missing mandatory metadata.

Failed subjects create a data-quality issue routed to Software Engineer; if a breaking schema change was published without notice, roll back the subject and open an SDLC-Exception ticket, 10-business-day remediation.
Field definitions come from the schema registry subject definitions (field names, types, doc strings) and the catalog's technical metadata; not re-typed by hand.
Reconcile registry subject count vs catalog dataset count for the domain; totals must match, with orphans reported to 0.

Acceptance: registry entries are 'current' when every active topic has a catalog-discoverable subject with owner, description, glossary link, and compatibility mode; evidence is the daily registry-to-catalog reconciliation report (delta 0) archived in the data catalog/quality tool.

checklist.value: Each active topic's schema subject is registered as a dataset in the data catalog with owner and steward assigned.

testing.value: Reconciliation report shows 0 active topics without a registered, catalog-visible subject.

checklist.value: Every subject carries technical metadata (type, compatibility, version) and business metadata (owner, description, glossary term).

testing.value: Catalog completeness report shows 100% of subjects with required technical+business metadata fields populated.

checklist.value: Subjects are discoverable by name, owner, and glossary term in the data catalog search.

answers.value: The full scope of the named release: all user stories/defects in the release version, the impacted services/components per the change record, and the risk-ranked feature list requiring functional, integration, regression, performance, and UAT coverage.
Plan governs the current release cycle; authored at sprint/release planning and re-approved if release scope changes materially.

Plan states, per risk area: test types, entry/exit criteria, environments, test-data source, coverage target (>= 80% line, >= 90% on critical paths), and defect-severity gate. A high-risk feature without an assigned test type fails plan review.
Every in-scope story/defect maps to at least one planned test case; traceability matrix shows 0 orphan requirements and 0 orphan test cases.
Approved test plan and traceability matrix stored on the Jira release version and Confluence 'Test Plan' page, version-stamped and timestamped; retained per release records policy.
Scope items deferred out of test coverage are logged with a risk-acceptance note and named approver on the Jira release; unresolved coverage gaps block plan approval.
Test strategy version is approved and recorded on the Confluence Test Plan page header; changes require re-approval by the Test Lead and Tech Lead before execution begins.

Risk-based sensitivity: features rated High risk require regression + integration + performance coverage; Medium require regression + integration; Low require regression. Thresholds documented in the plan's risk table.
Materiality gate: no Critical or High-severity open defects at release; up to 5 Medium defects allowed with documented workarounds and Product Owner sign-off.
All in-scope requirements and their mapped test cases in the traceability matrix for the release.
PASS = 100% of in-scope requirements traced to >= 1 test case, coverage targets set, and defect gate defined; FAIL if any requirement is untested or exit criteria are absent.
Gaps found in review reopen the plan for the Software Engineer/Test Lead, 3-business-day SLA; unresolved gaps escalate to the Release Manager and block the release gate.
Acceptance: plan is approved when the traceability matrix is complete, coverage and defect-severity gates are set, environments/test-data are named, and Test Lead + Tech Lead have signed off.
Approved plan on Confluence 'Release <version> Test Plan'; traceability matrix and approvals on the Jira release version; both linked from the release runbook.

Approved test strategy version and its parameter source (risk-ranking model + coverage thresholds) are recorded in the Test Plan page header; parameters sourced from the engineering testing standards, not ad hoc.

checklist.value: Plan allocates coverage across unit, integration, and end-to-end/UAT layers with the bulk at unit/integration level.

testing.value: Test-type counts in the plan follow a pyramid shape; an inverted (E2E-heavy) plan is rejected.

checklist.value: Plan mandates >= 80% line coverage on changed code, enforced later by the SonarQube quality gate.

testing.value: The SonarQube new-code coverage gate is set to 80% and referenced in the plan.

checklist.value: Plan identifies critical business paths (e.g., policy bind, claim FNOL) and targets >= 90% coverage on them.

testing.value: Every critical path in the risk table has assigned test cases meeting the 90% target.

checklist.value: Plan names the test-data source and masking approach for each environment; no unmasked production PII in test.

testing.value: Test-data provisioning records show masked/synthetic data for all lower environments.

answers.value: The named stream-processing job(s) requiring exactly-once semantics and late-arrival (watermark/allowed-lateness) handling: source topics, checkpointing config, transactional sink(s), and the windowing operators.
Configuration validated for the current release and re-validated on any change to sink, checkpoint interval, or watermark policy.

Job config sets processing.guarantee=exactly_once (or Flink checkpointing EXACTLY_ONCE) with a transactional/idempotent sink, defined watermark strategy, and allowed-lateness window. Missing any of these is a config failure caught in CI.

Under a duplicate-injection test, output record count equals distinct input event count (0 duplicates); under a delayed-event test, late events within the allowed-lateness window are counted and beyond it are routed to the side-output/DLQ.
Config-as-code committed to the source code/CI-CD repository with PR history; the exactly-once/late-arrival test report is attached to the merge and retained 12 months.
Events arriving beyond allowed lateness are written to a dead-letter/side-output topic and logged; a reconciliation job reports DLQ volume, disposition tracked in ServiceNow.

checklist.value: Sink writes are idempotent/transactional (upsert on event key or Kafka transactions) so replays do not duplicate output.

testing.value: Replaying a checkpoint produces identical sink state; output row count unchanged (0 duplicates).

checklist.step: Enforce data contracts on the stream
checklist.value: Input/output schemas are contract-validated at job boundaries; contract violations are rejected, not silently dropped.

testing.value: A malformed event is routed to the DLQ and does not corrupt exactly-once output.

checklist.value: An automated integration test exercises duplicate and late-arrival scenarios against a test broker in CI.

testing.value: CI integration suite passes duplicate-injection and late-event tests with the defined thresholds.

checklist.value: Checkpoint failures, DLQ volume, and watermark lag are alerted on in the observability stack.

testing.value: A DLQ spike triggers an alert with a linked runbook within 1 minute.

Environments provisioned for the current release test window; refreshed each release and torn down or reset after UAT sign-off.

Each environment provisioned from version-controlled IaC, config parity with production validated, masked test data loaded, and a post-provision smoke test passing. An environment failing smoke test is not released to QA.
Provisioned resource inventory matches the IaC plan output (terraform plan shows 0 drift); seeded test-record counts match the expected dataset manifest.
IaC state, terraform plan/apply logs, and the smoke-test report are stored in the source code/CI-CD repository and linked to the ServiceNow change ticket, timestamped and retained 12 months.
Provisioning failures or config drift are logged on the ServiceNow change ticket with disposition; environment blocked from QA use until drift = 0, owner = Software Engineer, 3-business-day SLA.
All environments provisioned for the release (SIT, UAT) and their seeded datasets and integration endpoints.
PASS = terraform plan shows 0 drift vs prod-parity baseline, smoke test green, and masked test data loaded to expected counts; FAIL on any drift, failed smoke test, or unmasked PII detected.
Failed provisioning reopens the change task for Software Engineer; if unmasked PII is detected, halt, purge the dataset, and open an SDLC-Exception ticket with a 24-hour remediation SLA.
Environment/config field definitions come from the IaC variable files and the CMDB environment CI records (tier, region, sizing), referenced not duplicated.
Reconcile provisioned resource counts and seeded record counts against the IaC plan and dataset manifest; both must match with 0 drift.

answers.value: All UAT scenarios for the release, mapped to business acceptance criteria, executed by named business stakeholders in the UAT environment; scope = every in-scope story requiring business validation.
UAT executed during the release UAT window (typically the final sprint before go-live); sign-off valid for the specific release version only.
Each UAT case records: scenario, tester, execution date, actual vs expected result, pass/fail, and linked defect if failed. A case with no recorded outcome fails the UAT completeness check.
Executed UAT case count equals planned UAT case count in the traceability matrix; unexecuted cases must be 0 or explicitly waived with business sign-off before closure.
UAT results, defects, and the signed acceptance form are captured on the Jira release version and Confluence UAT page, timestamped and version-stamped; retained per release records policy.
Failed UAT cases raise Jira defects with severity; Critical/High block sign-off; Medium/Low may be deferred with a Product Owner-approved risk note and target release.
All planned UAT scenarios for the release executed by business stakeholders in the UAT environment.
PASS = 100% of UAT cases executed with recorded outcomes and 0 open Critical/High defects; FAIL if any case is unexecuted or a Critical/High defect remains open at sign-off.
Failed cases reopen for the QA Analyst and dev team; blocking defects escalate to the Product Owner and Release Manager and hold the go-live gate until resolved or formally risk-accepted.
UAT expected-result definitions trace to the story acceptance criteria in Jira; testers validate against those criteria, not free interpretation.
Reconcile executed vs planned UAT case counts and pass/fail tallies in the traceability matrix; executed must equal planned (minus signed waivers).

testing.value: Release gate blocks until a completed, dated UAT sign-off record is present; verified by Jira automation.

answers.value: All critical integration points and data flows for the release in staging: Guidewire PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter/BillingCenter interfaces, partner APIs, ESB/Kafka flows, and downstream lakehouse loads exercised end-to-end.
Integration tests run in staging for the current release candidate; re-run on every deploy to staging until the release is promoted.

Each integration point has a contract test and an end-to-end data-flow test; request/response schemas validate, and payload field mappings match the interface spec. An untested critical interface fails the gate.
Records sent across each interface reconcile with records received downstream (e.g., policies bound in PolicyCenter equal rows landed in the lakehouse) within a 0% tolerance for critical flows.

Integration test run reports (pass/fail per interface), reconciliation output, and pipeline logs stored in the source code/CI-CD repository and linked to the compliance evidence repository; retained 12 months.
Failed interfaces raise Jira defects and block promotion; transient failures are retried once, persistent failures escalate to Integration Engineer, 3-business-day SLA, tracked on the change ticket.
Interface test approach/version is approved and recorded on the staging test plan; changes to contracts require re-approval by the Integration Architect before re-test.
Latency/throughput sensitivity documented per interface: p99 response time and max sustained TPS thresholds; breach flags a performance risk before promotion.
Materiality: any reconciliation discrepancy on a financial/policy-of-record flow is material and blocks release; non-critical reporting flows tolerate <= 0.1% variance with a logged note.
All critical integration points and their end-to-end data flows in the staging environment for the release.
PASS = 100% of critical interfaces pass contract + e2e tests and reconcile with 0 discrepancy on financial/PoR flows; FAIL on any contract break, failed e2e flow, or reconciliation mismatch.

Failures reopen for Integration Engineer/Software Engineer; unresolved critical failures escalate to the Release Manager and hold the promotion gate; an SDLC-Exception ticket is required to proceed with a known non-critical failure.
Acceptance: staging integration testing passes when every critical interface passes contract + end-to-end tests, reconciliation is clean on critical flows, and performance thresholds are met.
Test reports and reconciliation output on the CI run and the staging test plan; audit evidence copied to the compliance evidence repository and linked from the change ticket.
Pre/post comparison: downstream data state before and after the release flows is diffed; only intended changes appear, with row-count and key-field reconciliation passing.
The ServiceNow change ticket (CHG#) authorizing the staging deploy is linked in the CI run and the test report; test evidence is attached to that change record before promotion approval.

Approved interface-test methodology/version and its parameter source (contract specs + reconciliation rules) recorded on the staging test plan; parameters sourced from the interface specifications, not ad hoc.

Source-system field definitions come from the Guidewire/partner interface specs and schema registry; control totals reconcile source record counts (e.g., PolicyCenter transactions) against downstream landed counts per run.
